summary:
New Caledonia is a French collectivity. It stands under the French national framework: France retains responsibility for penal law, civil-status documents and the justice system, while the collectivity legislates locally on many domestic matters. The protections a trans visitor would rely on are French national provisions, applying here because French law governs.

The inventory records no New Caledonia-specific law, enforcement action, incident, institution or statistic bearing on trans visitors, and no local ordinance narrowing the national protections. No region-specific signal was identified, and the national assessment for France applies.
tangentialFactors:
The inventory's material from France, including the prison placement rule keyed to the recorded legal gender marker, the detention watchdog's findings on transgender detainees, the marriage-equality statute and the discrimination ground in the penal code, reaches New Caledonia only as an application of French law. It is carried by the France record and is not specific to this collectivity.

The inventory offers no comparison between New Caledonia and neighbouring jurisdictions in the region on any trans-relevant measure.
localsOnly:
The inventory records no New Caledonia-specific provision on legal gender recognition, gender-affirming care, employment protection or facility access for residents. Those matters are governed by French national law and are carried by the France record.

No New Caledonia-specific enforcement data, court decision or administrative practice concerning trans residents appears in the inventory.
outOfScopeNotes:
National French statistics on recorded anti-trans and homophobic violence carry no New Caledonia breakdown in the inventory. Whether the rate in the collectivity differs from the national figure is not sourced.

Whether any local ordinance, court ruling or administrative practice in New Caledonia touches legal gender recognition, care access or facility use is unresolved; the inventory contains no such material.
